<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

---
name: feedback-concurrent-agent-worktree-wipe
description: Concurrent automation deletes/guts worktrees + submodule checkouts; commit+push the submodule BEFORE any long verification
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 830d2806-d323-48b7-80b9-f28cf7556caf

---

On 2026-07-28 a concurrent agent/automation on this machine twice destroyed in-flight work in `.claude/worktrees/`: first it deleted the whole `activity-memory-split` worktree (uncommitted owletto changes lost, reconstructed from conversation context), later it gutted the recreated worktree down to `packages/owletto` and de-registered it (`git worktree list` no longer showed it; git commands inside fell through to the MAIN checkout — which it left sitting on a feature branch). Disk was also at 99% with the automation re-installing node_modules in worktrees as fast as caches were cleared.

**Why:** worktrees are shared mutable state between sessions; a cleanup/bump job prunes what looks stale, and uncommitted submodule changes don't make the outer worktree look dirty.

**How to apply:**
- In a submodule worktree, `git commit` + `git push -u origin <branch>` as soon as a coherent chunk exists — BEFORE running long gates. Pushed commits survived both wipes; working trees did not.
- If a worktree's git commands start reporting main-repo branches/paths, STOP — the worktree is orphaned and every git command is hitting `~/Code/lobu`.
- Recovery trick: a plain `git clone --reference-if-able ~/Code/lobu/.git/modules/packages/owletto` dropped into `packages/owletto` works fine in place of the submodule; and symlinking the worktree-root `node_modules` to the main checkout's resolves the workspace deps without a 2GB install.
- Disk full on this box: safe reclaims are worktree `node_modules`/`dist`, `~/.bun/install/cache`, `~/Library/Caches/{bun,ms-playwright,org.swift.swiftpm}`.

cat > /tmp/pr-body-schema.md <<'BODY'
## Summary
- `scripts/review.sh` hands one schema file to both reviewer CLIs, but they do not accept the same dialect. `claude --json-schema` refuses a `$schema` meta-reference and exits **before reading the prompt**; codex ignores the key.
- So the repo only broke on the claude fallback — which is exactly where it lands during a codex quota outage, with no second reviewer left. `pi-review` is a required check with `enforce_admins` on, so this blocked every merge in the repo.
- The dialect declaration is optional metadata for both CLIs. Dropped it, and added a guard so it cannot come back silently.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `make test-unit`, targeted `bun test scripts/__tests__/review-output-schema.test.ts`
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: ran `./scripts/test-bot.sh` or relevant eval

### red — schema as it was on `main`

```
$ claude -p "…" --json-schema "$(cat prompts/review-output-schema.json)" --output-format text
Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema: no schema with key or ref "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
```

### green — same invocation with `$schema` removed

```
$ claude -p "…" --json-schema "$(jq 'del(."$schema")' prompts/review-output-schema.json)" --output-format text
{"bug_free_confidence":50,"bugs":0,"slop":0,"simplicity":50,"blockers":[],"change_type":"chore",
 "behavior_change_risk":"none","tests_adequate":true,"suggested_fixes":[],"notes":"test",
 "categories":{"src":0,"tests":0,"docs":0,"config":0,"deps":0,"migrations":0,"ci":0,"generated":0}}
```

A schema-valid verdict, which is what `review.sh` gates on.

### guard, mutation-tested

```
$ bun test scripts/__tests__/review-output-schema.test.ts
 6 pass  0 fail

# re-add "$schema" to the file:
(fail) review output schema stays loadable by both reviewer CLIs > declares no meta-schema reference claude cannot resolve
 5 pass  1 fail

# restore:
 6 pass  0 fail
```

## Notes
**codex evidence is partial, and I want that on the record.** codex is out of credits until Aug 5, so it could not round-trip the schema. What I did verify is that `codex exec --output-schema` accepts the file identically **with and without** the key — both runs get past local schema validation and die at the same quota error — so the local validation step is unaffected. The remote structured-output call is untested against the edited file.

The guard covers the two failure modes that misreport themselves: an unresolvable dialect ref (claude refuses the file) and a `required` name with no matching property (codex's strict mode rejects it). Both surface to the operator as "reviewer returned no schema-valid JSON verdict", which reads as a flaky model and sends the next person to re-run the review rather than to this file.

Found while shipping #2371, where it blocked the merge and I had to strip the key in the working tree to get a review at all.
BODY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-review fixer: runs the reviewer CLI over the local diff with WRITE
# access and prompts/review-fix-prompt.md, so review-grade findings get fixed
# BEFORE `make review` posts a pi-review status. Posts nothing; commits
# nothing. The driving agent inspects the edits (shown at the end), commits,
# then runs `make review` once on the settled HEAD.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

BASE_BRANCH="${BASE:-}"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --base)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "usage: scripts/review-fix.sh [--base <branch>]" >&2; exit 2; }
      BASE_BRANCH="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    *)
      echo "usage: scripts/review-fix.sh [--base <branch>]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$BASE_BRANCH" ]; then
  if git rev-parse --verify --quiet origin/main >/dev/null; then
    BASE_BRANCH="origin/main"
  else
    BASE_BRANCH="main"
  fi
fi

git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$BASE_BRANCH^{commit}" >/dev/null \
  || { echo ">> invalid base ref '$BASE_BRANCH'" >&2; exit 2; }
git merge-base "$BASE_BRANCH" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || { echo ">> no merge base between '$BASE_BRANCH' and HEAD" >&2; exit 2; }

PROMPT_FILE="prompts/review-fix-prompt.md"
[ -f "$PROMPT_FILE" ] || { echo ">> missing $PROMPT_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }

if git diff --quiet "$BASE_BRANCH...HEAD" 2>/dev/null && git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo ">> no diff against $BASE_BRANCH and no local changes; nothing to fix"
  exit 0
fi

command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo ">> codex not found on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }

LAST_MSG_FILE="$(mktemp /tmp/lobu-review-fix.XXXXXX)"
trap 'rm -f "$LAST_MSG_FILE"' EXIT

echo ">> pre-review fixer (codex, base $BASE_BRANCH) — edits the working tree, posts nothing"
CODEX_ARGS=(codex exec --sandbox workspace-write --output-last-message "$LAST_MSG_FILE" --ephemeral)
if [ -n "${CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL:-}" ]; then
  CODEX_ARGS+=(--model "$CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL")
fi

set +e
env BASE_BRANCH="$BASE_BRANCH" "${CODEX_ARGS[@]}" "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")" < /dev/null > /dev/null
FIXER_EXIT=$?
set -e

echo
echo "========== fixer summary =========="
if [ -s "$LAST_MSG_FILE" ]; then
  cat "$LAST_MSG_FILE"
else
  echo "(no summary emitted)"
fi
echo "==================================="
echo
echo ">> working-tree changes made by the fixer (staged + unstaged; verify before committing):"
git status --short
git diff --stat HEAD
exit "$FIXER_EXIT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-review fixer: runs the reviewer CLI over the local diff with WRITE
# access and prompts/review-fix-prompt.md, so review-grade findings get fixed
# BEFORE `make review` posts a pi-review status. Posts nothing; commits
# nothing. The driving agent inspects the edits (shown at the end), commits,
# then runs `make review` once on the settled HEAD.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

BASE_BRANCH="${BASE:-}"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --base)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "usage: scripts/review-fix.sh [--base <branch>]" >&2; exit 2; }
      BASE_BRANCH="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    *)
      echo "usage: scripts/review-fix.sh [--base <branch>]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$BASE_BRANCH" ]; then
  if git rev-parse --verify --quiet origin/main >/dev/null; then
    BASE_BRANCH="origin/main"
  else
    BASE_BRANCH="main"

  || { echo ">> invalid base ref '$BASE_BRANCH'" >&2; exit 2; }

  || { echo ">> no merge base between '$BASE_BRANCH' and HEAD" >&2; exit 2; }

[ -f "$PROMPT_FILE" ] || { echo ">> missing $PROMPT_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }

name: project_review_harness_codex_single_point
description: "The review harness silently collapses when codex is down: $schema made the claude reviewer unusable and review-fix.sh had no claude path at all — PR #2372"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Codex ran out of credits 2026-07-30 (returns Aug 5) and the whole review harness went with it, in two
independent ways that both hid themselves.

**1. `prompts/review-output-schema.json` declared `$schema: draft/2020-12`.** `scripts/review.sh` hands
ONE schema file to both CLIs, but `claude --json-schema` cannot resolve that meta-reference and exits
before reading the prompt:

    Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema: no schema with key or ref
    "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"

codex ignores the key, so this only broke on the claude fallback — exactly where you land during a codex
outage, with no second reviewer left. `pi-review` is required with `enforce_admins` on, so it blocked
every merge in the repo. It surfaces as "reviewer returned no schema-valid JSON verdict", which reads as
a flaky model and sends you to re-run the review rather than to the file.

**2. `scripts/review-fix.sh` was hard-wired to codex** (`command -v codex || exit 1`) while `review.sh`
already honoured `REVIEWER_CLI=auto|codex|claude`. `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review-fix` was accepted and
silently ignored. Worse than the first: review-fix posts no status, so an outage does not fail a check —
the mandated step (AGENTS.md "Ship a change" #5) just doesn't happen and nothing records it.

**How to apply:** when a gate suddenly "fails for no reason", check whether the harness has a
single-CLI dependency before re-running it. `REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=fable` is the
override; `auto` deliberately picks the OTHER CLI so a model never grades its own diff.

**Codex evidence is partial and stayed that way.** With no credits, codex could not round-trip the
edited schema. What was verified: `codex exec --output-schema` accepts the file identically with and
without the key (both get past local validation and die at the same quota error). The remote
structured-output call is untested — re-verify after Aug 5.

Related: [[reference_review_harness_quota_and_schema_traps]], [[feedback_use_fable_for_review]],
[[reference_pi_review_env_blocker_deadlock]], [[project_behavior_version_skill_snapshots]].

## Summary
The review harness has two independent single-points-of-failure on codex, and both hide themselves. Codex ran out of credits today, which surfaced them together.

**1. `prompts/review-output-schema.json` declared `$schema: draft/2020-12`.** `scripts/review.sh` hands one schema file to both reviewer CLIs, but `claude --json-schema` cannot resolve that meta-reference and exits **before reading the prompt**; codex ignores the key. So the repo only broke on the claude fallback — exactly where it lands during a codex outage, with no second reviewer left. `pi-review` is required with `enforce_admins` on, so this blocked every merge.

**2. `scripts/review-fix.sh` was hard-wired to codex** (`command -v codex || exit 1`) while `review.sh` already honoured `REVIEWER_CLI=auto|codex|claude`. `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review-fix` was accepted and silently ignored. This one is worse than a broken gate: review-fix posts no status, so an outage doesn't fail a check — the mandated step (AGENTS.md "Ship a change" #5) just doesn't happen, and nothing records that a quality pass was skipped.

Same class — the review tooling must survive either CLI being down — so they ship together.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `make test-unit`, `bash scripts/lib/__tests__/review-reviewer.test.sh`, `bun test scripts/__tests__/review-output-schema.test.ts`
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: ran `./scripts/test-bot.sh` or relevant eval

```

Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema: no schema with key or ref "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"

{"bug_free_confidence":50,"bugs":0,"slop":0,"simplicity":50,"blockers":[],"change_type":"chore",

```

A schema-valid verdict, which is what `review.sh` gates on.

ERROR: You've hit your usage limit … try again at Aug 5th

>> pre-review fixer (claude, base origin/main) — edits the working tree, posts nothing
========== fixer summary ==========
Fixer pass complete. All touched tests green …

Structural assertions went into `scripts/lib/__tests__/review-reviewer.test.sh` rather than a new file: it already holds the identical class of greps for `review.sh` and already runs in CI, and it already covers selector/model-allowlist *behavior*, so a separate TS test would have been two homes for one thing.

description: "Behavior skills are pinned as {name,content} snapshots on watcher_versions.skills and delivered as .skills/ files — #2371 MERGED + PROD-VERIFIED, but INERT from the web UI until owletto stops compiling skills into prompt"

**#2371 — merged 2026-07-30, squash `84b86a6a724d6d07264083005ca2f49d48ad3bc4`, LIVE on prod
image `20260730-220649-001763`.** Gate run and opened: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 84b86a6a <deployed>`.

**What changed.** Skills used to be concatenated into `watcher_versions.prompt` at save time, which
discarded the seams — no diff, no upgrade, no picker rehydration, and `prompt` owned by the compiler.
Now `watcher_versions.skills` (jsonb) holds `[{name, content}]` pinned snapshots, `prompt` goes back to
being the author's task statement, and the instruction rule is **prompt OR ≥1 skill** (see
`assertBehaviorInstructions`, `packages/server/src/behaviors/triggers.ts`). NULL = pre-column version;
`[]` = authored with skills, none chosen.

Delivery is split by path and that divergence is deliberate: server runs get the snapshots as a
`.skills/*/SKILL.md` tree via `resolveBehaviorRunSkills` (`gateway/behavior-run-session.ts`), device
runs get them composed into the dispatch payload at `worker-api/poll.ts`, chat-listen keeps the live
library.

**PROD-VERIFIED (closure) 2026-07-30.** `behavior_versions.skills` is selectable through the MCP
allowlist against prod — one query proves BOTH the migration applied AND the `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA`
registration landed. All rows NULL, which is correct: nothing writes snapshots yet (below). Pods
2/2 Running, 0 restarts, zero `malformed pinned skills` hits in logs.

**THE HALF THAT IS STILL MISSING — the web UI does not use any of this.**
`packages/owletto/src/lib/behavior-skills.ts` still exports `compileBehaviorInstructions`, and
`from-scratch-panel.tsx` still joins skill bodies into `prompt` and sends **no** `skills` array. So
#2371 is exercised only by `lobu apply` and the MCP tools; every Behavior authored in the browser
still writes the old shape. Not a regression — but do not read "shipped" as "reachable from the UI".
The owletto work owed: add `skill` to `LobuRefKind` (`src/lib/references.ts`), `@` chips in the prompt
composer, and turn `behavior-skills-picker.tsx` from an editor into a read-only attached strip hosting
the diff/upgrade action. Design settled with the user as **"Chips only"**.

**Traps that nearly shipped, none caught by unit tests:** the migration had no `-- migrate:up`/`down`
markers (column existed locally only because it was applied by hand — under the real runner it would
have created nothing anywhere); `resolveBehaviorRunSkills`'s SQL had never touched Postgres because the
gateway test injects a fake `db` returning a canned row; and storing without delivering would have been
worse than not shipping, since every existing declarative Behavior is skills-only and the write half
alone would have emptied their instructions on the next `lobu apply`.

tokens are `@[kind:id:label](path)` and the server ALREADY derives `sources[]` from them server-side
(`extractSourcesFromPromptTokens` + `PROMPT_KIND_TO_MODE`, `watchers/source-refs.ts`) — so a `skill`
token could plausibly be derived the same way. It must NOT be: deriving it means the server reads the
skill body at save time, which is exactly what `assertBehaviorSkillsResolve` deliberately refuses to do
(it validates the NAME and stores the CALLER's content, so a re-save can never silently upgrade a pin).
Do **not** add `skill` to `PROMPT_KIND_TO_MODE` — skills are not sources.

Chosen: **the composer resolves chips into `skills[{name,content}]` and sends both**, server write path
unchanged — PLUS a fail-closed guard that rejects a prompt carrying a `@[skill:…]` token with no
matching entry in `skills[]`. Without that guard the MCP/CLI mismatch (token in prompt, no array)
degrades to inert literal text in the agent's instructions, silently.

Related: [[project_issue_2320_thin_skills_triage]], [[project_behavior_skill_merge_rejected]],

description: "Behavior skills are pinned as {name,content} snapshots on watcher_versions.skills and delivered as .skills/ files — #2371 MERGED + PROD-VERIFIED, but INERT from the web UI until owletto stops compiling skills into prompt"

**#2371 — merged 2026-07-30, squash `84b86a6a724d6d07264083005ca2f49d48ad3bc4`, LIVE on prod
image `20260730-220649-001763`.** Gate run and opened: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 84b86a6a <deployed>`.

**What changed.** Skills used to be concatenated into `watcher_versions.prompt` at save time, which
discarded the seams — no diff, no upgrade, no picker rehydration, and `prompt` owned by the compiler.
Now `watcher_versions.skills` (jsonb) holds `[{name, content}]` pinned snapshots, `prompt` goes back to
being the author's task statement, and the instruction rule is **prompt OR ≥1 skill** (see
`assertBehaviorInstructions`, `packages/server/src/behaviors/triggers.ts`). NULL = pre-column version;
`[]` = authored with skills, none chosen.

Delivery is split by path and that divergence is deliberate: server runs get the snapshots as a
`.skills/*/SKILL.md` tree via `resolveBehaviorRunSkills` (`gateway/behavior-run-session.ts`), device
runs get them composed into the dispatch payload at `worker-api/poll.ts`, chat-listen keeps the live
library.

**PROD-VERIFIED END-TO-END (closure) 2026-07-30.** Two independent proofs:

1. `behavior_versions.skills` is selectable through the MCP allowlist against prod — one query proves
   BOTH the migration applied AND the `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA` registration landed. All rows NULL, correct:
   nothing writes snapshots yet (below).
2. **A real Behavior ran on the new code.** Behavior 71 fired 22:25 UTC, run 810538, and logged the
   exact new seam: `Session context for watcher_71: … 0 chars skills instructions, … 0 skills
   (Behavior run — pinned snapshot), provider: gemini`, then `Created API agent:
   personal-agent_watcher_71_run_810538`. `resolveBehaviorRunSkills` resolved, returned empty for a
   NULL-skills version, and the run proceeded. `next_run_at` advanced 22:25 → 23:25.

Pods 2/2 Running, 0 restarts, zero `malformed pinned skills` hits.

Two log-reading traps hit while verifying, both worth reusing:
- `kubectl logs -l <selector> --max-log-requests=N` **silently returned nothing** here while looping
  over pod names returned the lines. Always iterate pods by name.
- `[worker-auth] Error verifying token` bursts look alarming and are **benign**: worker-token
  verification is tried first, fails for an external OAuth token, and `external-auth-client` discovery
  succeeds right after ("Fetched external auth user info"). Not a failure — a noisy auth-chain fallback.

Unrelated oddity noticed, NOT caused by this change: `behaviors.last_fired_at` stays NULL for 71 even
though it demonstrably fired and rescheduled. Behavior 5 shows the same (last fired 2026-07-19).

**THE HALF THAT IS STILL MISSING — the web UI does not use any of this.**
`packages/owletto/src/lib/behavior-skills.ts` still exports `compileBehaviorInstructions`, and
`from-scratch-panel.tsx` still joins skill bodies into `prompt` and sends **no** `skills` array. So
#2371 is exercised only by `lobu apply` and the MCP tools; every Behavior authored in the browser
still writes the old shape. Not a regression — but do not read "shipped" as "reachable from the UI".
The owletto work owed: add `skill` to `LobuRefKind` (`src/lib/references.ts`), `@` chips in the prompt
composer, and turn `behavior-skills-picker.tsx` from an editor into a read-only attached strip hosting
the diff/upgrade action. Design settled with the user as **"Chips only"**.

**Traps that nearly shipped, none caught by unit tests:** the migration had no `-- migrate:up`/`down`
markers (column existed locally only because it was applied by hand — under the real runner it would
have created nothing anywhere); `resolveBehaviorRunSkills`'s SQL had never touched Postgres because the
gateway test injects a fake `db` returning a canned row; and storing without delivering would have been
worse than not shipping, since every existing declarative Behavior is skills-only and the write half
alone would have emptied their instructions on the next `lobu apply`.

[[project_skills_as_entity_and_agent_installs]], [[feedback_post_merge_prod_verify_wakeup]].

content.text:
Integration is the last check. While it finishes — the design fork for the owletto half, which I resolved before writing any UI code:

Prompt `@` tokens already get turned into `sources[]` **server-side** (`extractSourcesFromPromptTokens`), so the obvious move would be to derive `skills` the same way. That's wrong, and it took reading `source-refs.ts` to see why: deriving server-side means the server reads the skill body at save time — exactly what `assertBehaviorSkillsResolve` refuses to do. It validates the *name* and stores the *caller's* content, precisely so a re-save can never silently upgrade a pin. Deriving would reintroduce the bug #2371 was built to prevent.

So: the composer resolves chips into `skills[{name,content}]` and sends both, server write path unchanged — plus a fail-closed guard rejecting a prompt that carries a `@[skill:…]` token with no matching array entry. Without that guard, an MCP or CLI caller who writes the token but omits the array gets the literal token as inert text in the agent's instructions, silently.

Session context for watcher_71: … 0 chars skills instructions, …
0 skills (Behavior run — pinned snapshot), provider: gemini
```

`resolveBehaviorRunSkills` resolved against a NULL-skills version, returned empty, and the run proceeded to `Created API agent: personal-agent_watcher_71_run_810538`. That plus the live `behavior_versions.skills` query covers both the storage and delivery halves.

**#2372 — reviewed clean, 8/9 checks green.** `pi-review pass`, 0 bugs, 0 blockers, risk low — and it ran through the claude reviewer, which is the fix demonstrating itself. The fixer pass on this branch caught that my guard test was wired into no CI step, and corrected a false claim I'd written about `$defs`/`$ref`; I verified its consolidation rather than trusting the self-report.

**Confidence: 95 on #2371** — live run through the changed code path plus a live schema query. **90 on #2372** — real red→green through the harness, mutation-tested guards, full CI; the codex remote call stays untested until Aug 5.

**Next actions:**
1. **Merge #2372** when integration reports — I'll do this automatically.
2. **Build the owletto composer** with the design above: `skill` in `LobuRefKind`, chips in the prompt field, picker demoted to a read-only strip with the upgrade action, plus the fail-closed guard. This is the work that makes #2371 reachable from the browser, and it owes before/after screenshots.
3. **Optionally tighten the schema guard** to walk nested keys — the reviewer's one suggestion. Low value given nested `$ref` isn't actually a failure mode, so I'd fold it into another PR rather than spend a review cycle.
4. **`behaviors.last_fired_at` never gets stamped** — 71 demonstrably fired and rescheduled but the column stayed NULL, and behavior 5 shows the same since July 19. Unrelated to this work, but it makes the Behaviors UI under-report and is worth a look.

33	entry, then the transaction:false lock fix). Both were correct and both were
34	UNVERIFIED — it cannot run Postgres. Re-verify anything it pushes; `git log
35	--format=%cn` before assuming your own commit is the head. See
36	[[reference_squash_merge_breaks_ancestry_checks]] for the merge-SHA gate.

40	`transcript-routes.ts` (`stampBehaviorLastRun`), `agent-thread-list.ts` (union
41	from watchers), and 2 test files. `make pre-pr` clean.

43	## THE BUG THE E2E CAUGHT — two run-id spaces
44	
45	**One Behavior execution writes TWO `runs` rows.** The `run_type='behavior'`
46	job's id is what gets packed into the conversation id as `_run_<id>`; the
47	`run_type='chat_message'` turn the dispatcher queues for it is what the worker
48	token and the snapshot POST body carry. Measured live: conversation
49	`owletto-default_watcher_1_run_109` checkpoints under `runId=112`.
50	
51	review-fix's `intent.runId !== args.runId` guard (which the earlier note here
52	told me to KEEP) compares those two spaces, so it can never be true —
53	`stampBehaviorLastRun` was dead code and Behaviors would have vanished from the
54	listing entirely. Fix: drop the comparison. `isRunOwnedByJwtScope` already binds
55	the conversation id to the authenticated run, and the UPDATE re-fences org+agent,
56	so the behaviorId parsed out of the verified conversation id is trustworthy.
57	
58	The unit test agreed with the bug: its fixture built the conversation id from the
59	same runId it minted the token with, so the two spaces coincided — a shape
60	production never produces. See [[feedback_test_the_shape_production_throws]].
61	Fixture now inserts both rows. Mutation-tested (broken guard → 1 fail).
62	
63	Live red→green on `:9186`, same request both times:
64	RED `200 {"id":1}` + `last_run_completed_at` NULL;
65	GREEN `200 {"id":1}` + `2026-07-30 20:08:41.374+01`.
66	Then: `GET /lobu/api/v1/agents/<id>/history/threads?scope=all` returns the three
67	Behaviors ordered by the stamp, and archiving one drops it from the listing while
68	its stamp stays — the prod bug, fixed. Recorded: artifact
69	https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f78dc2b1-5d85-4adf-8ae8-77fb1b265f22
70	
71	**No LLM run completed locally — every provider key is exhausted** (Anthropic no
72	credit, Z.ai weekly limit, Gemini 429, OpenRouter 402, OpenAI 400 on
73	`reasoning_effort` + function tools for gpt-5.6-sol). Five real Behavior runs
74	dispatched, all five failed at the model — which incidentally proved the negative
75	case (failed checkpoints never stamp). The checkpoint POST was driven directly
76	with a minted worker token; that IS the code under test.
77	
78	**No UI on this branch consumes `scope=all`** — the Recent sidebar lives on the
79	unmerged owletto `feat/restore-recent-list`. Nothing to film here.
80	
81	## The bug
82	
83	`agent-thread-list.ts` derived Behavior rows at read time: leading-wildcard
84	`LIKE '%\_watcher\_%\_run\_%'` + per-row `regexp_match` + `GROUP BY` over
85	`agent_transcript_snapshot`, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable,
86	grows with run history forever.
87	
88	Worse, it was unfixably stale: archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past
89	runs, so the derive path had nothing to filter on. **22 of personal-agent's 26
90	Behavior rows in prod were archived Behaviors it could never drop** (prod:
91	4 active / 56 archived org-wide).
92	
93	## REJECTED approach (already built — do not resurrect)
94	
95	Gave Behaviors a `conversations` row keyed `behavior:<id>`, kind `'behavior'`,
96	plus a trigger on `watchers` to sync name/status/agent_id. It worked and passed
97	every gate, but needed: a CHECK-constraint widening, a DB trigger, a
98	`FOR UPDATE` race guard, three `kind <> 'behavior'` leak guards in
99	`findConversationById`/`getConversation`/admin scope, and a fix for a
100	listing-row-strands-on-agent-reassignment bug **that the design itself created**.
101	Half the mechanism defended against problems the design introduced — the
102	coordination-brake smell. Behaviors are not conversations.
103	
104	## ACCEPTED approach
105	
106	One column on the bounded config table, then union at read time.
107	
108	- `ALTER TABLE watchers ADD COLUMN last_run_completed_at timestamptz`
109	- partial index `(organization_id, agent_id, last_run_completed_at DESC)
110	  WHERE status='active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL`
111	  (squawk needs a `-- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation`; watchers
112	  is ~60 rows in prod)
113	- **backfill reads `runs`, NOT `agent_transcript_snapshot`** — no regexp, no
114	  LIKE, groups on a real FK:
115	  `SELECT watcher_id, max(completed_at) FROM runs WHERE run_type='behavior' AND
116	  status='completed' AND watcher_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY watcher_id`
117	- write: `transcript-routes.ts`, same completed-checkpoint site, single-row
118	  `UPDATE watchers SET last_run_completed_at = GREATEST(...)`. **Keep
119	  review-fix's `intent.runId !== args.runId` guard.**
120	- read: bounded select on watchers; `status`/`name` read LIVE so archive and
121	  rename need NO sync at all — that is where all the deleted machinery goes.
122	- `conversations-store.ts` reverts fully to `origin/main`.
123	
124	**Do NOT check `last_fired_at` or `updated_at` as the timestamp** — measured on
125	prod: `last_fired_at` is NULL on every Behavior that ran today (it is
126	event-cooldown bookkeeping) and `updated_at` tracks scheduler/definition writes,
127	disagreeing with the listing on 3 of 4 active Behaviors.
128	
129	## Keep from the rejected branch
130	
131	The AGENTS.md invariant, the deletion of the derive block, and the red→green
132	test `drops an archived Behavior even though its completed runs remain` (its
133	assertion holds under either design; proved red against
134	`git show origin/main:...agent-thread-list.ts`). Delete the
135	agent-reassignment test — that bug cannot exist when the row IS the watcher.
136	
137	## Gotchas hit
138	
139	- `behaviors` is NOT a view: `table-schema.ts:422` is an explicit column
140	  allow-list mapping to physical `watchers` (`['behaviors','watchers']` at :745).
141	  A new column is NOT auto-exposed to `query_sql` — opt in deliberately.
142	- **The vitest/bun harness re-runs migrations on startup**, so mutating a
143	  trigger via `psql` is silently reverted before the test runs and yields a
144	  meaningless pass. Mutate the migration FILE instead. See
145	  [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]].
146	- Changing an already-applied migration needs the test DB recreated
147	  (`dropdb/createdb lobu_test` + `CREATE EXTENSION vector, cube, earthdistance`).
148	- squawk lints the **down** path too — `constraint-missing-not-valid` fired on a
149	  plain `ADD CONSTRAINT` there. CI pins `squawk-cli@2.58.0
150	  --exclude=ban-drop-column,require-timeout-settings`; `bunx squawk@latest` is a
151	  DIFFERENT, unrelated package.
152	- Test fixture traps: `watchers.created_by` is FK-constrained to `"user"`, and
153	  `idx_runs_executing_per_behavior` allows only one in-flight run per Behavior,
154	  so a helper that checkpoints twice must settle each run first.
155	
156	## Unverified
157	
158	Prod row counts for `runs` / `agent_transcript_snapshot` — neither is in the MCP
159	query allowlist. dbmate wraps migrations in a transaction, so **size them before
160	shipping the backfill**.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

content.text:
Fair challenge, and the honest answer is: **the guard is enforcement, but I was about to let it paper over a real question I hadn't settled.** Let me separate the two.

The guard itself is legitimate in the same way `assertBehaviorSkillsResolve` is — the prompt is free text, so "every chip has a pinned body" isn't expressible in a type, and the repo's rule is to fail closed at the write path. That part I'd defend.

What's *not* settled is why there are two representations that can disagree at all. Three options:

**Derive skills from prompt tokens server-side** — one source of truth. I rejected this and I still would, for two concrete reasons: it forces the server to read skill bodies at save time, which silently upgrades pins (exactly what #2371 exists to prevent), and it breaks skills-only declarative Behaviors — `defineBehavior({ skills: [...] })` with no prompt would resolve to zero skills and strand every CLI-authored Behavior. That's the failure mode I caught before shipping #2371.

**Chips are the only way to attach a skill** — the array becomes a pure rendering of the prompt. Clean, but it deletes the declarative path for the same reason.

**Array is authoritative, chips are a rendering of it** — what I'm building. The composer keeps them in sync; the guard catches callers that don't.

So: not a workaround, but the guard is *detection*, and the actual prevention lives in the composer. The asymmetry I should have stated outright is that it's deliberately one-directional — a pinned skill with **no** chip is allowed, because that's precisely the declarative/CLI case. A chip with no pin is an error because it degrades to literal `@[skill:…]` text in the agent's instructions.

If you'd rather skills only ever come from chips, that's a coherent design too — but it means dropping `skills:` from `defineBehavior`, and that's a contract change worth deciding deliberately rather than as a side effect of this PR.

I'll proceed with the array-authoritative model and the one-directional guard. Want me to reconsider if you were pointing at option 2?

cat > /tmp/pr2373.md <<'BODY'
## Summary
Completes #2371. That PR made the server store and deliver pinned skill snapshots; nothing in the browser wrote them — `owletto/src/lib/behavior-skills.ts` still compiled skill bodies into `prompt` and sent no `skills` array, so the feature was reachable only from `lobu apply` and MCP. This adds the composer (owletto#661) and the one server-side guard it needs.

**The guard.** Nothing strips ref tokens — grep `PROMPT_REF_TOKEN`, the only consumer is source derivation — so a `@[skill:…]` chip with no matching entry in `skills[]` does not fail, it **degrades**: the agent reads the literal `@[skill:deploy-runbook:Deploy runbook](/…)` as if it were guidance, with no `.skills/` file behind it. Silent wrong instructions are worse than a 422.

Checked at both write paths (`create`, `create_version`), **names only**. The pinned body still comes from the caller — resolving it here would re-read the live library at save time and silently upgrade a pin, which is exactly what the snapshot model exists to prevent.

**Deliberately one-directional.** A pinned skill with *no* chip is legal: that is the declarative path (`defineBehavior({ skills: [...] })` carries no prompt at all), and rejecting it would strand every CLI-authored Behavior.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `make test-unit`, `bun test src/__tests__/unit/prompt-skill-tokens-pinned.test.ts` (11), `behavior-instructions-rule.test.ts` (5); owletto `bunx vitest run` — 129 files / 1138 tests
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: ran `./scripts/test-bot.sh` or relevant eval

### Guard, mutation-tested

```
$ bun test src/__tests__/unit/prompt-skill-tokens-pinned.test.ts
 11 pass  0 fail

# mutate: `if (referenced.length === 0) return` -> `>= 0` (guard never fires)
 7 pass  4 fail        <- exactly the four rejection cases

# restored
 11 pass  0 fail
```

The four that fail are the ones that matter: a chip with no pin, several unpinned chips named together, a *partially* pinned set (the realistic drift — composer sent a stale array after one more chip was added), and a chip whose id differs from its label, which must be checked on the id or a rename shows green while pinning the wrong body.

### The bug the old regression test caught in my own draft

owletto#634 added a test asserting an author with an empty skill library gets a link to the skills page. My first draft rendered that link only in the `else` of the validation error — and an empty library and an unsatisfied instruction requirement co-occur on **every blank new-Behavior form**. So the link vanished exactly when it was needed, which is the same stranding #634 wrote the test for. Fixed in the component, not the test.

## Notes
**This is the second half of a two-PR change; merge owletto#661 first.** The pointer bump is in this PR.

Design decision worth recording: prompt chips are a *rendering* of the `skills[]` array, not an independent declaration. The alternative — deriving `skills` from prompt tokens server-side, one source of truth — was rejected because it forces a save-time read of skill bodies (silently upgrading pins) and resolves skills-only declarative Behaviors to zero skills. That second failure mode is the one caught before shipping #2371.

Also verified while closing out #2371: it is live on prod and a real Behavior ran through the new path — `Session context for watcher_71: … 0 skills (Behavior run — pinned snapshot)`, run 810538.

3	description: "Booting a task worktree for browser/e2e testing: build-packages (not build), make dev serves only the API, the SPA is a separate vite with LOBU_API_PROXY, and how to drive an agent-attributed tool call without an LLM"
4	metadata:

10	
11	The exact sequence to get a `make task-setup` worktree testable in a browser. Verified 2026-07-29 in `.claude/worktrees/merge-snapshot-evidence` (PORT=9143). Each step below cost a wasted round-trip when skipped.
12	
13	**1. `make build` is a NO-OP — the target you want is `make build-packages`.**
14	`make build` prints "Nothing to be done for `build'" and exits 0, which looks like success. A fresh worktree has no `packages/*/dist`, so until you run `make build-packages` vitest dies at import time with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@lobu/pgvector-embedded"` and then `Failed to load url @lobu/core/contracts/interaction-envelope`. Both are the same missing-dist cause wearing different messages. Related: [[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]], [[reference_empty_worktree_node_modules_resolves_main]].
15	
16	**2. `make dev` boots ONLY the API.** It runs `packages/server` (`tsx watch src/server.ts`) on the worktree's `.env.local` PORT. It does **not** serve the SPA — `/` and `/index.html` 404 (health reports `"mode":"cloud"`, and in cloud mode the frontend is hosted separately). `packages/owletto/dist/index.html` existing does not change this. Editing server TS is live via tsx watch; no restart needed.
17	
18	**3. The SPA is a second process — vite — and must use `LOBU_API_PROXY`, not `VITE_API_URL`.**
19	```
20	cd packages/owletto && LOBU_API_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<API_PORT> \
21	  bun run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port <pick a free one>
22	```
23	`prodApiProxy()` in `vite.config.ts` same-origin-proxies `/api`, `/oauth`, `/connect` and rewrites Set-Cookie (drops Domain, SameSite=None→Lax) so better-auth sessions work. `VITE_API_URL` does NOT work for auth — the config comments say so explicitly.
