name: reference_worktree_dev_boot_recipe
description: "Booting a task worktree for browser/e2e testing: build-packages (not build), make dev serves only the API, the SPA is a separate vite with LOBU_API_PROXY, and how to drive an agent-attributed tool call without an LLM"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: c3dc213c-a275-44a5-9345-8bf68a35760f
  modified: 2026-07-29T15:52:45.643Z
---

The exact sequence to get a `make task-setup` worktree testable in a browser. Verified 2026-07-29 in `.claude/worktrees/merge-snapshot-evidence` (PORT=9143). Each step below cost a wasted round-trip when skipped.

**1. `make build` is a NO-OP — the target you want is `make build-packages`.**
`make build` prints "Nothing to be done for `build'" and exits 0, which looks like success. A fresh worktree has no `packages/*/dist`, so until you run `make build-packages` vitest dies at import time with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@lobu/pgvector-embedded"` and then `Failed to load url @lobu/core/contracts/interaction-envelope`. Both are the same missing-dist cause wearing different messages. Related: [[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]], [[reference_empty_worktree_node_modules_resolves_main]].

**2. `make dev` boots ONLY the API.** It runs `packages/server` (`tsx watch src/server.ts`) on the worktree's `.env.local` PORT. It does **not** serve the SPA — `/` and `/index.html` 404 (health reports `"mode":"cloud"`, and in cloud mode the frontend is hosted separately). `packages/owletto/dist/index.html` existing does not change this. Editing server TS is live via tsx watch; no restart needed.

**3. The SPA is a second process — vite — and must use `LOBU_API_PROXY`, not `VITE_API_URL`.**
```
cd packages/owletto && LOBU_API_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<API_PORT> \
  bun run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port <pick a free one>
```
`prodApiProxy()` in `vite.config.ts` same-origin-proxies `/api`, `/oauth`, `/connect` and rewrites Set-Cookie (drops Domain, SameSite=None→Lax) so better-auth sessions work. `VITE_API_URL` does NOT work for auth — the config comments say so explicitly.

**4. The SPA's backend is the ORIGIN. `/lobu` is the Agent API gateway only.**
Setting `VITE_API_URL=.../lobu` yields `GET /lobu/api/auth-config 404` and a "Not signed in" page. Measured on the live server:
```
/api/auth-config       -> 200
/lobu/api/auth-config  -> 404
```
See [[project_embedded_server_lobu_prefix]] — this is the same split, and it bites the SPA config too.

**5. Dev DB is per-branch on 127.0.0.1:5418** (brew postgresql@18), named `lobu_<branch with / and - as _>` — e.g. branch `feat/merge-snapshot-evidence` → `lobu_feat_merge_snapshot_evidence`. Find it with `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -l`. A fresh one has 1 org (`local-install`), 1 user, 0 events — so an empty Activity page is EXPECTED, not a bug. Agents `lobu-builder` + `owletto-default` are seeded, but `inference_providers` is empty, so chat may not resolve a model (see [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]]).

**6. Integration tests** want `lobu_test`, which is also reachable on 5418:
```
cd packages/server && DATABASE_URL="postgres://$USER@127.0.0.1:5418/lobu_test" PGSSLMODE=disable \
  node ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path> -t "<name>"
```

**7. To exercise an AGENT-attributed tool call without wiring an LLM** — the useful trick, since the LLM only decides *to call* the tool and everything under test is downstream. Mint a PAT straight into the dev DB (`token = "owl_pat_" + randomBytes(24).toString("base64url")`, `token_hash = sha256(token)` hex, `token_prefix = token.slice(0,12)`, scope `'mcp:read mcp:write mcp:admin'`), then do the MCP streamable-HTTP handshake against `POST /mcp/<orgSlug>`:
`initialize` → read the `mcp-session-id` response header → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/call`. Send `x-lobu-agent-id: <agentId>` on every call. `classifyMutationPrincipal` gives `agentId` precedence over `userId`, so the context resolves to kind `"agent"` and takes the approval-gated branch instead of the human fast path. Skipping the handshake returns `Bad Request: Server not initialized`.

Do NOT sign in / create the local account yourself — that's the user's step.

empty-library link sat in the `else` of the validation error, and those two states co-occur on every
blank form, so the link vanished exactly when needed.

in `skills[]`. Nothing strips ref tokens, so an unpinned chip degrades to literal

pinned skill with no chip is the declarative path and must stay legal. Consequence for `lobu apply`:
a config prompt with a hand-written chip not listed in `skills:` now 422s instead of shipping a dead

name: project_behavior_version_skill_snapshots
description: "Behavior skills are pinned as {name,content} snapshots on watcher_versions.skills and delivered as .skills/ files — #2371 MERGED + PROD-VERIFIED, but INERT from the web UI until owletto stops compiling skills into prompt"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 30140936-8f87-43bd-83a7-fe289633e312
  modified: 2026-07-30T22:32:18.106Z
---

**#2371 — merged 2026-07-30, squash `84b86a6a724d6d07264083005ca2f49d48ad3bc4`, LIVE on prod
image `20260730-220649-001763`.** Gate run and opened: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 84b86a6a <deployed>`.

**What changed.** Skills used to be concatenated into `watcher_versions.prompt` at save time, which
discarded the seams — no diff, no upgrade, no picker rehydration, and `prompt` owned by the compiler.
Now `watcher_versions.skills` (jsonb) holds `[{name, content}]` pinned snapshots, `prompt` goes back to
being the author's task statement, and the instruction rule is **prompt OR ≥1 skill** (see
`assertBehaviorInstructions`, `packages/server/src/behaviors/triggers.ts`). NULL = pre-column version;
`[]` = authored with skills, none chosen.

Delivery is split by path and that divergence is deliberate: server runs get the snapshots as a
`.skills/*/SKILL.md` tree via `resolveBehaviorRunSkills` (`gateway/behavior-run-session.ts`), device
runs get them composed into the dispatch payload at `worker-api/poll.ts`, chat-listen keeps the live
library.

**PROD-VERIFIED END-TO-END (closure) 2026-07-30.** Two independent proofs:

1. `behavior_versions.skills` is selectable through the MCP allowlist against prod — one query proves
   BOTH the migration applied AND the `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA` registration landed. All rows NULL, correct:
   nothing writes snapshots yet (below).
2. **A real Behavior ran on the new code.** Behavior 71 fired 22:25 UTC, run 810538, and logged the
   exact new seam: `Session context for watcher_71: … 0 chars skills instructions, … 0 skills
   (Behavior run — pinned snapshot), provider: gemini`, then `Created API agent:
   personal-agent_watcher_71_run_810538`. `resolveBehaviorRunSkills` resolved, returned empty for a
   NULL-skills version, and the run proceeded. `next_run_at` advanced 22:25 → 23:25.

Pods 2/2 Running, 0 restarts, zero `malformed pinned skills` hits.

Two log-reading traps hit while verifying, both worth reusing:
- `kubectl logs -l <selector> --max-log-requests=N` **silently returned nothing** here while looping
  over pod names returned the lines. Always iterate pods by name.
- `[worker-auth] Error verifying token` bursts look alarming and are **benign**: worker-token
  verification is tried first, fails for an external OAuth token, and `external-auth-client` discovery
  succeeds right after ("Fetched external auth user info"). Not a failure — a noisy auth-chain fallback.

FALSE POSITIVE I raised and retract: NULL `behaviors.last_fired_at` on a Behavior that demonstrably
fired. That column is event-cooldown bookkeeping, never stamped on the schedule path;
`last_run_completed_at` (added by #2370, already merged and deployed) is the real "last ran" column and
IS populated on prod. See [[project_behavior_listing_column]], which had already measured this.

**THE HALF THAT IS STILL MISSING — the web UI does not use any of this.**
`packages/owletto/src/lib/behavior-skills.ts` still exports `compileBehaviorInstructions`, and
`from-scratch-panel.tsx` still joins skill bodies into `prompt` and sends **no** `skills` array. So
#2371 is exercised only by `lobu apply` and the MCP tools; every Behavior authored in the browser
still writes the old shape. Not a regression — but do not read "shipped" as "reachable from the UI".
The owletto work owed: add `skill` to `LobuRefKind` (`src/lib/references.ts`), `@` chips in the prompt
composer, and turn `behavior-skills-picker.tsx` from an editor into a read-only attached strip hosting
the diff/upgrade action. Design settled with the user as **"Chips only"**.

**Traps that nearly shipped, none caught by unit tests:** the migration had no `-- migrate:up`/`down`
markers (column existed locally only because it was applied by hand — under the real runner it would
have created nothing anywhere); `resolveBehaviorRunSkills`'s SQL had never touched Postgres because the
gateway test injects a fake `db` returning a canned row; and storing without delivering would have been
worse than not shipping, since every existing declarative Behavior is skills-only and the write half
alone would have emptied their instructions on the next `lobu apply`.

**Design fork resolved for the owletto half (2026-07-30), before writing any UI code.** Prompt `@`
tokens are `@[kind:id:label](path)` and the server ALREADY derives `sources[]` from them server-side
(`extractSourcesFromPromptTokens` + `PROMPT_KIND_TO_MODE`, `watchers/source-refs.ts`) — so a `skill`
token could plausibly be derived the same way. It must NOT be: deriving it means the server reads the
skill body at save time, which is exactly what `assertBehaviorSkillsResolve` deliberately refuses to do
(it validates the NAME and stores the CALLER's content, so a re-save can never silently upgrade a pin).
Do **not** add `skill` to `PROMPT_KIND_TO_MODE` — skills are not sources.

Chosen: **the composer resolves chips into `skills[{name,content}]` and sends both**, server write path
unchanged — PLUS a fail-closed guard that rejects a prompt carrying a `@[skill:…]` token with no
matching entry in `skills[]`. Without that guard the MCP/CLI mismatch (token in prompt, no array)
degrades to inert literal text in the agent's instructions, silently.

Related: [[project_issue_2320_thin_skills_triage]], [[project_behavior_skill_merge_rejected]],
[[project_skills_as_entity_and_agent_installs]], [[feedback_post_merge_prod_verify_wakeup]].

Review and CI are both running on the settled HEAD. I'll merge when they report.

The fixer pass earned its keep again — it found that **my own branch invalidated a claim I'd written in it.** The guard test's header said `PROMPT_REF_TOKEN` had exactly one consumer (source derivation); adding `extractSkillNamesFromPromptTokens` made that a second one, so the comment was stale on the very tree that introduced it. It also enumerated every write path to confirm the guard covers the class — `handleUpdate` can't touch prompt/skills, `handleCreateFromVersion` copies a stored pair verbatim, and the two non-handler `INSERT INTO watcher_versions` sites write server-owned prompts with no chips.

I corrected one thing it got wrong: it claimed the pointer bump carries exactly one owletto commit. That was true when it started and stale when it reported — it began before I merged #661 and repointed. The bump actually spans seven commits, including #660 (a Mac TCC fix from another lane) and five bot image bumps. Bumping onto *current* main is right, but I've disclosed the span on the PR rather than letting a reviewer discover #660 in the diff.

Its residual-risk note is worth repeating because I agree with the judgment: a pre-existing version whose prompt hand-typed a `@[skill:…]` token would now 422 on a metadata-only version bump. Chips only ship with this branch's composer, so such a row would have to be a deliberate forgery — same shape as how `assertBehaviorInstructions` was introduced.

**Confidence: high (90) on the server guard** — 11 tests, mutation-verified with all four rejection cases failing when disabled, write paths enumerated, `pre-pr` and unit green. **Medium-high (75) on the composer** — 1138 owletto tests pass and it caught a real bug in my draft, but nobody has looked at the rendered form and chip insertion is exercised via `prefill` rather than by typing into ProseMirror.

**After merge, still owed:** before/after screenshots (needs your sign-in), and a prod-verify — this changes what every Behavior save accepts, so it deserves the live check rather than assuming.

**#2371 — merged 2026-07-30, squash `84b86a6a724d6d07264083005ca2f49d48ad3bc4`, LIVE on prod
image `20260730-220649-001763`.** Gate run and opened: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 84b86a6a <deployed>`.

**What changed.** Skills used to be concatenated into `watcher_versions.prompt` at save time, which
discarded the seams — no diff, no upgrade, no picker rehydration, and `prompt` owned by the compiler.
Now `watcher_versions.skills` (jsonb) holds `[{name, content}]` pinned snapshots, `prompt` goes back to
being the author's task statement, and the instruction rule is **prompt OR ≥1 skill** (see
`assertBehaviorInstructions`, `packages/server/src/behaviors/triggers.ts`). NULL = pre-column version;
`[]` = authored with skills, none chosen.

Delivery is split by path and that divergence is deliberate: server runs get the snapshots as a
`.skills/*/SKILL.md` tree via `resolveBehaviorRunSkills` (`gateway/behavior-run-session.ts`), device
runs get them composed into the dispatch payload at `worker-api/poll.ts`, chat-listen keeps the live
library.

**PROD-VERIFIED END-TO-END (closure) 2026-07-30.** Two independent proofs:

1. `behavior_versions.skills` is selectable through the MCP allowlist against prod — one query proves
   BOTH the migration applied AND the `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA` registration landed. All rows NULL, correct:
   nothing writes snapshots yet (below).
2. **A real Behavior ran on the new code.** Behavior 71 fired 22:25 UTC, run 810538, and logged the
   exact new seam: `Session context for watcher_71: … 0 chars skills instructions, … 0 skills
   (Behavior run — pinned snapshot), provider: gemini`, then `Created API agent:
   personal-agent_watcher_71_run_810538`. `resolveBehaviorRunSkills` resolved, returned empty for a
   NULL-skills version, and the run proceeded. `next_run_at` advanced 22:25 → 23:25.

Pods 2/2 Running, 0 restarts, zero `malformed pinned skills` hits.

Two log-reading traps hit while verifying, both worth reusing:
- `kubectl logs -l <selector> --max-log-requests=N` **silently returned nothing** here while looping
  over pod names returned the lines. Always iterate pods by name.
- `[worker-auth] Error verifying token` bursts look alarming and are **benign**: worker-token
  verification is tried first, fails for an external OAuth token, and `external-auth-client` discovery
  succeeds right after ("Fetched external auth user info"). Not a failure — a noisy auth-chain fallback.

FALSE POSITIVE I raised and retract: NULL `behaviors.last_fired_at` on a Behavior that demonstrably
fired. That column is event-cooldown bookkeeping, never stamped on the schedule path;
`last_run_completed_at` (added by #2370, already merged and deployed) is the real "last ran" column and
IS populated on prod. See [[project_behavior_listing_column]], which had already measured this.

field: prose plus `@[skill:…]` chips, resolved to `skills[{name, content}]` at save. `skill` joins

**The component already existed and I nearly rebuilt it from scratch.** `template-fields-editor.tsx`
(the Goal field, `@`-mention + SQL dialog) was deleted by owletto **#634 on the same day**; `git show
262d75af^:…` recovers it, and its wiring (focus-ring wrapper, `[&_.ProseMirror]:min-h-[7rem]`,
`submitOnEnter={false}`, `handleRef`) is better than a fresh draft. The stale docstring in
`use-mention-search.ts` still says "shared by the chat composer and the watcher prompt editor" — that
second consumer had been deleted. **A docstring naming a consumer is not evidence the consumer
exists; grep for it.** #634's own regression test then caught a real bug in the redraft: the
empty-library link sat in the `else` of the validation error, and those two states co-occur on every
blank form, so the link vanished exactly when needed.

**Server guard added (#2374):** `assertPromptSkillTokensPinned` rejects a chip with no matching entry
in `skills[]`. Nothing strips ref tokens, so an unpinned chip degrades to literal
`@[skill:…](…)` text in the agent's instructions rather than failing. ONE-directional by design — a
pinned skill with no chip is the declarative path and must stay legal. Consequence for `lobu apply`:
a config prompt with a hand-written chip not listed in `skills:` now 422s instead of shipping a dead
reference; the CLI does not scan prompts for chips.

**THE ORIGINAL GAP (now closed) — the web UI did not use any of this.**
`packages/owletto/src/lib/behavior-skills.ts` still exports `compileBehaviorInstructions`, and
`from-scratch-panel.tsx` still joins skill bodies into `prompt` and sends **no** `skills` array. So
#2371 is exercised only by `lobu apply` and the MCP tools; every Behavior authored in the browser
still writes the old shape. Not a regression — but do not read "shipped" as "reachable from the UI".
The owletto work owed: add `skill` to `LobuRefKind` (`src/lib/references.ts`), `@` chips in the prompt
composer, and turn `behavior-skills-picker.tsx` from an editor into a read-only attached strip hosting
the diff/upgrade action. Design settled with the user as **"Chips only"**.

**Traps that nearly shipped, none caught by unit tests:** the migration had no `-- migrate:up`/`down`
markers (column existed locally only because it was applied by hand — under the real runner it would
have created nothing anywhere); `resolveBehaviorRunSkills`'s SQL had never touched Postgres because the
gateway test injects a fake `db` returning a canned row; and storing without delivering would have been
worse than not shipping, since every existing declarative Behavior is skills-only and the write half
alone would have emptied their instructions on the next `lobu apply`.

**Design fork resolved for the owletto half (2026-07-30), before writing any UI code.** Prompt `@`
tokens are `@[kind:id:label](path)` and the server ALREADY derives `sources[]` from them server-side
(`extractSourcesFromPromptTokens` + `PROMPT_KIND_TO_MODE`, `watchers/source-refs.ts`) — so a `skill`
token could plausibly be derived the same way. It must NOT be: deriving it means the server reads the
skill body at save time, which is exactly what `assertBehaviorSkillsResolve` deliberately refuses to do
(it validates the NAME and stores the CALLER's content, so a re-save can never silently upgrade a pin).
Do **not** add `skill` to `PROMPT_KIND_TO_MODE` — skills are not sources.

Chosen: **the composer resolves chips into `skills[{name,content}]` and sends both**, server write path
unchanged — PLUS a fail-closed guard that rejects a prompt carrying a `@[skill:…]` token with no
matching entry in `skills[]`. Without that guard the MCP/CLI mismatch (token in prompt, no array)
degrades to inert literal text in the agent's instructions, silently.
